Rows you leave out stay UNADJUDICATED and are scored nowhere -- nothing here is ever defaulted. The rows waiting for you are in ai-causation-2026-08.review.md. To send a row back to UNADJUDICATED, delete the line. Confirm the lot in one edit: `sed -i '' 's/"rec:/"/' docs/recall-reference-sets/ai-causation-2026-08.adjudications.json`. Then set _confirmed_by to your name and run `python3 railway/ab_ai_causation.py --rescore`.

_the_ruling: THE SPEAKER QUESTION IS ANSWERED. ai_explicit requires THE EMPLOYER to have attributed the cuts to AI. A report counts when it quotes or reports the employer saying it. A journalist's own characterisation, with no such statement from the employer, is the BROAD tier ('ai_linked'), not this one. The rule is now stated for readers on the methodology page (#m-ai), asked for in extractor.ai_causation_prompt() and SYSTEM_PROMPT rule 2, and described in alt_allowed_ai_causation(). It is no longer derived across three files and stated in none.

All six speaker rows (70293 Snap, 70653 TikTok, 54973 Microsoft/MSN, 48830 Suncor, 70683 ByteDance/TikTok, 70681 TikTok) were confirmed FALSE on 2026-08-19 under the owner's deferral -- see _confirmed_by for exactly what he authorised. Each was re-read against #m-ai before confirming and none carries an employer attribution in its stored text: 70293 is a headline ('AI push leads to 1,000 job cuts') plus a reporter's summary; 70653 is a third party's claim ('It also claims that TikTok is looking to replace...'); 54973 is The Verge's framing ('The layoffs are part of a bigger push by Microsoft to rely on AI'); 48830 is the reporter's generic 'Driverless technology is only just starting to cause layoffs' with a union in the headline; 70683 is a 'sources say' headline where the company confirmed only the count; 70681 is a press purpose clause where the company confirmed the layoffs and not the reason. ONE CAVEAT TRAVELS WITH 70293 AND IS NOT A GOLD-SET DOUBT: the gold set judges the stored snippet, and on the snippet it is unambiguously false, but the LIVE row's ai_language carries an Evan Spiegel memo quote -- the employer's own words -- that appears nowhere in that row's own source text. The speaker rule therefore does NOT mechanically condemn the live row, and it was deliberately left out of the 2026-08-19 corrections pass. See TECHLOG.
_the_ruling_skill_swap: THE 'AI SKILLS SWAP' QUESTION IS ANSWERED, and 107375 (General Motors) is FALSE. GM cut hundreds of IT workers in order to hire people with stronger AI skills. GM's own words name AI, so the speaker ruling does not dispose of it; the separate question is what 'AI caused these cuts' means when nobody was replaced by a machine. THE TEST THE OWNER ACCEPTED: did the work go away, or did the required skill change? If a system now does the work, that is an AI layoff. If the same work still needs doing by different people, that is restructuring. GM is the second: the IT work continued and only the skill profile demanded of the people doing it changed, so AI is the reason the hiring bar moved, not the reason the work stopped. Ruled by the owner 2026-08-19. The rule is stated for readers on the methodology page (#m-ai) beside the speaker rule, so it is no longer a comment in a JSON file; that is the mistake the speaker question exposed. It settles a recurring shape and should be applied to the next 'cut to re-hire for AI skills' row without re-litigation.
